---
title: Items and types
description: An item is one thing a person keeps, such as a photo, a note or a contact, and its type says what the item holds. Everything else in Marfa builds on these two ideas.
job: A builder learns what an item is, what its type promises, who adds types where, and how an item moves from active to purged.
kind: concept
---

Everything in an instance is an item: a PDF, a photo, a contact, a conversation. Every item has a type, and **Marfa holds every item to its type**: every app that reads a `core.file.image` knows it will find a `blob_ref` and a `mime_type`, because Marfa refused any image without them.

Every item also has the same fixed fields, such as `id`, `state`, `version` and its three timestamps. The Catalog's [Items](/catalog/items) page lists them.

## What a type does

A type is the schema for an item's properties. It names each property, gives its kind, and says which ones are required. Marfa **checks every write** against it, so this image, which names no bytes, is refused with `400 invalid_properties`:

```http title="Request"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "type": "core.file.image", "properties": { "title": "Kitchen before the move" } }
```

**A property the type doesn't declare is kept**, unless the owner turns on `strict_mode` for the type in [Settings](/reference/instance-settings#enforcement-levers).

A type also tells an app how to show its items, through **display hints**: the field that names an item, the field that holds its Markdown text, and an icon such as `lucide:calendar`. [Type definition](/catalog/type-definition#display-hints) has the rules.

The Catalog's [Types](/catalog/types) page lists the types Marfa ships. When none fits, [define a type](/build/define-a-type).

## Who adds types where

A type's ID is two or more lowercase segments separated by dots. The first, its **namespace**, says who adds types there:

| Namespace | Example | Who adds types |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core`, `system` and `marfa` | `core.note`, `system.view` | Marfa. No one can change them. |
| `common` | `common.ticket` | Only a [plugin](/use/install-a-plugin), for types many apps share. |
| `app` | `app.readinglist.entry` | An app, for its own machinery. Always three segments. |
| `user` | `user.recipe` | You, or any credential granted write on `user.*`. |
| Any other root | `acme.deal` | Anyone publishing types for others, such as a connector. |

The second segment of an `app` type is its **vendor**. **A vendor belongs to the app that registered its first type**, which then reaches it without naming it; another app reaches it only through a grant that names `app.<vendor>.*`. A vendor the owner started is held for the owner, who can [give a vendor to another app or delete its data](/use/manage-app-data). [Access](/build/access) has the rules.

Items of a `system` or `app` type are **hidden**: listings, searches, counts and views leave them out unless a request names the type exactly or asks for `include=hidden`. The bin, exports and backups hold them.

## Building on another type

A type can name a **parent**. It then has every property the parent has, and adds its own. `core.file.image` is a child of `core.file`: it has a file's `blob_ref` and `mime_type`, and adds `width` and `height`.

**A listing of a type includes every type beneath it**, so an app that lists files finds your receipts among them. Inherit only when every property of the parent fits your type, because a child can't reshape what it inherits.

<TypeInheritance />

## Where an item came from

Every item records its **source**, a code for what wrote it, which never changes. An item can also carry a `source_id`, its own ID at that source, such as an event's ID in Google Calendar. **Together they are its natural key**: a connector that writes the record again updates the item instead of making a second one.

### Library and feed

Items sit in one of two **tiers**. The **library** holds what a person chose to keep. The **feed** holds what arrives in volume from elsewhere, such as an RSS connector's posts, until someone acts on it or its type's feed window moves it to the bin.

An item a connector keeps in step with another service answers `read_only: true`. **It's advice, not a lock:** an app uses it to warn before an edit.

## An item's life

An item starts `active`. **Archiving** sets it aside: listings leave it out unless asked, and it stays readable by its `id`.

<ItemLifecycle />

### Delete and purge

**A delete is a soft delete:** it moves the item to the bin, which the API calls the trash, with its children by `parent-of` and its [parts](/build/edges#parts). A restore brings them back.

**Purging** an item in the bin deletes it and its history for good, with `items.purge` and write on its type. The bin empties itself after `trash_retention_days`, 60 days by default.

The rules behind this page are in the [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md) and [types](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/types.md) chapters of the contract.
